A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DynaProt and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Existing material can be matched across the revised formatting and section numbering, and the additional appendix figures are available for inspection.

before.justification: v1 reports original DynaProt evaluations on ATLAS, a cryptic-pocket case study, BPTI ensemble generation, and loss-function and architecture ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds a multi-protein cryptic-pocket evaluation and analyses of ATLAS conformational trajectories.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the eight-block IPA backbone, marginal and pairwise Cholesky readouts, log-Frobenius objective, joint-covariance reconstruction heuristic, and Gaussian sampling procedure. The new evaluations do not introduce a method component or adaptation.

E1.justification: Figure 9 adds evaluation on BioEmu's reference cryptic-pocket protein set, with 33 labeled proteins, extending the existing adenylosuccinate-synthetase case study to a broader protein population. ATLAS training/evaluation and BPTI coverage remain unchanged; Figures 10–11 analyze existing ATLAS data.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 2–6 is unchanged, including FlexPert-3D, NMA, AFMD+Templates, ConfDiff, AlphaFlow-MD, BioEmu, ESM3, and ESMDiff in their respective comparisons. Figure 9 uses BioEmu's reference proteins but does not report a new comparison against BioEmu predictions.

E3.justification: Figure 9 introduces mean cosine alignment between predicted marginal principal axes and apo-to-holo displacement directions at annotated pocket residues. Figure 10 adds per-protein two-component PCA and density-derived free-energy visualization. Existing ATLAS splits, 250-structure ensemble evaluations, and established metrics are retained.

E4.justification: Supplementary analysis expands substantially beyond the original qualitative single-pocket example: Figure 9 quantitatively tests predicted pocket-opening directions across 33 proteins. Figures 10–11 additionally examine conformational basins and opening motions in ATLAS trajectories. The existing loss/IPA ablations and BPTI analysis remain unchanged.

E5.justification: The same three ATLAS simulation replicates and percentile summaries are described. Neither version reports model-seed uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests, and the added pocket-alignment plot introduces no uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Existing numerical tables and prediction plots retain their results. Figure 9 adds per-protein mean directional-alignment scores spanning approximately 0.22–0.81; Figure 10 adds nine conformational landscapes, and Figure 11 shows opening motions for 6q9c_A and 6y2x_A. These are supplementary outcomes, not improvements in previously reported benchmark scores.

T1.justification: The Gaussian definitions, reconstruction formula, SPD-closure proposition, sampling property, Appendix A.1 proofs, and Appendix A.2 metric derivations are unchanged. The added empirical analyses introduce no new formal result or mathematical argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about directly learning marginal and pairwise dynamics, parameter efficiency, predictive accuracy, and fast approximate ensemble generation. The new appendix evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v1 explicitly suggests predicting a structure from sequence before applying DynaProt; v2 omits this applicability suggestion. Existing interpretations and qualifications concerning backbone-only modeling, approximate joint reconstruction, generative-model limitations, and preliminary cryptic-pocket utility remain.

D1.justification: The new figure captions provide limited processing details: apo inputs and annotated pocket-residue displacements for Figure 9, and per-protein PCA followed by density-to-free-energy processing for Figure 10. Existing implementation disclosures remain unchanged, with no additional training hyperparameters, hardware specifications, or code-access information.

R1.justification: v2 removes the AlphaFold 3 citation and associated sequence-to-structure applicability discussion. Appendix A.3.3 newly emphasizes NMA as DynaProt's 'true comparison.' Most sequence-method discussion is relocated from the experimental setup, rather than newly added, and the remaining cited works are retained.

P1.justification: Most prose is retained, with localized wording edits, removal of the separate Setup heading, experimental subsection renumbering, and relocation of sequence-baseline discussion to Appendix A.3.3. The author affiliations and conference header are updated.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a different document-wide conference layout, redesigning the title and headings and resizing or relocating numerous displays, notably the wrapped Figure 2. Table 4 loses its second-best underlining, and three substantive appendix displays are added: the alignment bar chart, nine-panel landscape figure, and opening-motion illustrations.

improvement.justification: Figure 9 provides quantitative evidence across multiple proteins beyond v1's single visual cryptic-pocket example, while Figures 10–11 document ATLAS conformational diversity. These additions modestly strengthen empirical support. Their limited discussion, lack of a comparator or uncertainty for pocket alignment, and sparse processing details constrain the gain; the main method, results, and theoretical support remain unchanged.
